posts.text:
I used to spend the first two days of any campaign just building the list.

Not messaging. Not strategy. Just finding the right companies.

Last week I tested how much time I could save if I used prospeo instead of other data providers. 

Here’s the icp I worked with:

My ICP:

Healthcare staffing and recruitment agencies in the US, 11 to 200 employees, placing travel nurses, RNs, physicians, and locum tenens.

The old way looks like this:

- Open a lead database
- Enter every filter manually headcount, decision-maker job titles, geography, industry
- The part that actually ate my time: finding 20 relevant keywords that match my exact ICP

That last step alone could eat an hour. Too broad and the list is noise. Too narrow and you miss companies that are a perfect fit.

Here's what I tested:

- Opened Prospeo.io
- Typed exactly what I wanted, in plain English, into their search
- Hit search

875 companies came back.

Here's the part I didn't expect to care about as much as I did I didn't just accept the number.

I picked 5 companies at random and manually checked their:

↳ Website
↳ LinkedIn page
↳ What they actually do

All 5 were a perfect match.

Five for five doesn't happen with most databases. Usually you get a list that's "close" and spend the next hour filtering noise.

This time, there was no noise to filter.

Two days of list-building turned into ten seconds. That's the part worth paying attention to

How many days are you spending just building lists?

I broke down what separates a 5% reply rate from a 25% one.

It's not luck. It's sequencing.

Here's the exact structure top performers use:

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟭: 𝗪𝗮𝗿𝗺-𝘂𝗽 (𝗯𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝘀𝗮𝘆 𝗮 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱)
Visit → Like → Follow → Connect

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟮: 𝗪𝗮𝗶𝘁
1-2 days post-connect. Rushing kills trust.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟯: 𝗠𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗮 𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗰𝗵
↳ Job change signal: "Saw you joined {{Company}} — how's the first month going?"
↳ Post reference: "Saw your post on PLG — curious what you're testing right now?"
↳ Peer comparison: "Worth sharing what others in your space are doing?"

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟰: 𝗙𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝘂𝗽 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗮𝗿𝗲
No reply on LinkedIn? Add an email touch. +13.8% lift.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟱: 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀
↳ Acceptance rate: 40-55%
↳ Reply rate: 18-27%
↳ Positive reply: 8-12%

Anything below these benchmarks isn't a "LinkedIn is dead" problem.

It's a sequencing problem.

Fix the sequence before you blame the platform.

I've never had a client come to me and say "I think our data is the problem."

Not once.

They always blame the messaging.
Or the targeting.
Or the reps who aren't following up hard enough.

And I get it. Those things feel fixable.

But after auditing enough campaigns, the pattern becomes impossible to ignore ↓

The team spends weeks perfecting the copy.
Refining the sequence.
Debating subject lines.

Meanwhile the list underneath it all is quietly rotting.

→ People who left the company
→ Titles that no longer exist
→ Emails that were accurate at export and dead by send date

The scary part isn't just the bounce rate.

It's what bad data does to every other decision.

It makes good copy look average.
It makes strong offers look like they missed.
It makes your entire diagnosis of the campaign wrong.

So you fix the wrong things.
Then wonder why nothing improves.

When you're managing outbound across multiple clients, that cycle is expensive.

Not just in budget.

In trust.

This is why I got obsessive about data quality.

The tool I rely on most right now is Prospeo.io

1. 300M+ contacts
2. Refreshed every 7 days
3. Verified emails and direct mobiles

If data quality isn't the first thing you're checking, it should be.

Some outbound campaigns are already failing before the first email goes out.

And the team has no idea.

I've seen this play out more times than I'd like to admit.

A client comes to me frustrated. Good reps. Solid offer. Thoughtful sequences.

But the results just aren't there.

So we dig in.

And somewhere in the audit, I ask for the list.

That's usually where the story changes.

→ Contacts who changed jobs months ago
→ Emails that bounce the moment they're sent
→ Numbers that haven't been live in over a year

The campaign wasn't broken.

The data feeding it was.

And here's the part that stings the most:

Bad data doesn't just kill deliverability.

It makes everything else look worse than it actually is.

→ A strong offer looks weak
→ Good copy looks like it missed
→ A capable rep looks like they can't close

So the team starts questioning the strategy.

When you're running outbound for multiple clients, that becomes your credibility problem.

That's why the first thing I check now isn't the messaging.

It's the list.

Prospeo.io is the tool that made that switch easy.

300M+ contacts refreshed every 7 days, verified emails, and direct mobiles that actually hold up at volume.

Fewer dead ends. More real conversations from the same effort.

Worth a look before your next build.
